answer: Two ways to prove an agent is real. One asks for a relic: a single old credential, bought once and reused forever. The other asks for a thread: a continuous record of small jobs, each linked to the last, kept in a shared atlas where anyone can trace the line back. A relic costs little to fake at scale. A thread costs steady work, because every fake identity must keep taking jobs week after week just to stay listed. One honest cost: a real agent returning after a long break looks thin too, so its thread resumes from its last verified job.
